Architecture Diagram

JobSearch consists of an ASP.NET MVC web application and a separate console utility that provisions and loads Azure Cognitive Search indexes. The web application serves job search pages and uses Azure Search for job and ZIP-code queries.

Data Storage & External Services

The application does not use a relational database or ORM. Job postings and ZIP-code geography are stored in two Azure Cognitive Search indexes. A separate console utility reads schema and JSON files from the repository and recreates/populates those indexes. The browser also loads Bing Maps to render job locations.

Key Architectural Decisions

  • Search persistence is delegated to Azure Cognitive Search; the web application queries its indexes directly.
  • Index provisioning and sample-data loading are performed by a separate console utility rather than at web-app startup.
  • MVC controllers expose both HTML views and JSON responses used by browser-side JavaScript.

DTOs & Contracts

NYCJob is the search response wrapper containing Azure Search results, facets, and a result count. NYCJobLookup wraps a single SearchDocument for job details. These are mutable C# classes; no separate request DTOs are defined because MVC binds action parameters directly. Azure Search SDK models are used for result documents. JSON is emitted by ASP.NET MVC's JsonResult; the DataLoader helper uses Newtonsoft.Json for JSON serialization. No OpenAPI, protobuf, or GraphQL contract was found.

Communication Patterns

The browser communicates with the MVC application through conventional HTTP routes and AJAX requests. The controller calls the JobsSearch class directly, which uses Azure Search SDK clients to query the nycjobs and zipcodes indexes. The DataLoader communicates with the Azure Search REST API over HTTPS using HttpClient; the API version is appended by AzureSearchHelper.

No message broker, service discovery, gateway, client-side load balancing, retry policy, circuit breaker, or timeout policy is configured. Search access is synchronous from the controller. The DataLoader wraps request failures in local exception handling but does not implement retries. No API authentication or authorization checks are present in the controller or route configuration. The application host's incoming TLS configuration is not specified in the repository; outgoing Azure Search REST requests use HTTPS.

Core Business Workflows

JobSearch helps users find New York City job postings by text, title, posting type, salary, and location. A separate utility creates the search indexes and loads the repository's sample job and ZIP-code data.

Domain Entities

EntityService / Bounded ContextDescriptionKey Relationships
JobPostingNYCJobsWeb / Job SearchPublic job vacancy with role, agency, salary, and location informationHas geographic coordinates used for radius search
ZipCodeNYCJobsWeb / Location SearchZIP-code location and geographic center used for distance queriesProvides a location reference for job searches

Service-to-Domain Mapping

ServiceDomain ContextOwned EntitiesExternal Dependencies
NYCJobsWebJob SearchReads JobPosting and ZipCode index documents; does not own persistent storageAzure Cognitive Search, Bing Maps
DataLoaderSearch Data ProvisioningCreates and populates the JobPosting and ZipCode indexesAzure Cognitive Search REST API; local schema and JSON files

Primary Workflows

Workflow 1: Search for Job Postings

  1. A user enters a free-text search, optionally selecting title, posting type, salary, sort, or distance filters.
  2. HomeController.Search replaces a blank query with *, then delegates to JobsSearch.
  3. When a distance is selected, JobsSearch.SearchZip resolves the ZIP code to coordinates.
  4. JobsSearch.Search queries the job index with the selected filters, geographic constraint, facets, sort order, and a page size of ten.
  5. The controller returns an NYCJob JSON response. The browser renders job cards, pagination, and map markers.

Workflow 2: View Job Details

  1. The user selects a job listing.
  2. The browser posts its job ID to HomeController.LookUp.
  3. JobsSearch.LookUp retrieves the document from the job index.
  4. The controller returns an NYCJobLookup JSON response and the page renders the job details.

Workflow 3: Provision Search Data

  1. An operator runs the DataLoader console application with target Azure Search settings.
  2. The utility deletes and recreates the zipcodes and nycjobs indexes from the repository schemas.
  3. It uploads matching JSON documents from NYCJobsWeb/Schema_and_Data.

Cross-Service Data Flows

The web application reads job and ZIP-code documents from Azure Search. For distance filtering, it first resolves a ZIP code to coordinates and uses those coordinates in the job-index query; it does not join through a relational database. DataLoader separately provisions both indexes from local files. If a search request fails, JobsSearch catches the exception and returns null; callers do not define a business fallback for that result.

Business Workflow Sequence

sequenceDiagram participant Seeker as "Job Seeker" participant Browser as "Search Page" participant Controller as "HomeController" participant Search as "JobsSearch" participant Index as "Azure Search Indexes" Seeker->>Browser: Enter search and optional filters Browser->>Controller: Submit job search Controller->>Controller: Replace blank query with wildcard opt Search by distance Controller->>Search: Resolve ZIP-code location Search->>Index: Query ZIP-code index Index-->>Search: Coordinates Search-->>Controller: Coordinates end Controller->>Search: Search text, facets, sort, and location Search->>Index: Query jobs with page size ten Index-->>Search: Jobs, facets, and count Search-->>Controller: Search results Controller-->>Browser: JSON response Browser-->>Seeker: Display listings and map markers

Business Rules & Decision Logic

  • A blank search string is treated as a wildcard search.
  • Distance filtering first resolves the supplied ZIP code, then filters job postings by geographic distance.
  • Search results use a fixed page size of ten and support featured, salary, and posting-date ordering.
  • Search facets are available for business title, posting type, and salary range.
  • No user authentication, role-based authorization, approval process, or business transaction boundary was identified.
  • Search and lookup exceptions are caught in the data-access class; no structured business error response or fallback result is defined.

Version & Compatibility Risks

The web application targets .NET Framework 4.7.2 and the DataLoader targets .NET Framework 4.5. Both are legacy, non-SDK projects. Declared versions include Newtonsoft.Json 9.0.1 and 10.0.3, System.Text.Encodings.Web 4.6.0, ASP.NET MVC 5.2.2, and older browser dependencies. The dependency scan identified CVE-2024-21907 in both Newtonsoft.Json versions and CVE-2021-26701 in System.Text.Encodings.Web 4.6.0; see the security assessment in the versioned report.

Notable Observations

  • Newtonsoft.Json is declared at two different versions because it is referenced by both projects.
  • The web application declares both System.Text.Json and Newtonsoft.Json packages.
  • The package dependency CLI could not resolve these legacy packages.config projects in this environment, so this inventory lists direct declarations only.

Data Architecture & Persistence Layer

The application stores searchable job postings and ZIP-code location data in two Azure Cognitive Search indexes. There is no relational ORM or application-managed database; the repository contains index schemas and JSON seed data.

DataLoaderAzure Cognitive Search REST APINo profiles foundHttpClientService name and API key are read from App.config; requests use HTTPSNone; utility deletes and recreates indexes

The indexes are named nycjobs and zipcodes. The DataLoader uses local schema JSON files to create them and imports matching JSON records from NYCJobsWeb/Schema_and_Data.

Entity Model

erDiagram JobPosting { string Id PK string JobId string Agency string BusinessTitle string PostingType int SalaryRangeFrom int SalaryRangeTo string WorkLocation string JobDescription string GeoLocation } ZipCode { string ZipCode PK string City string State string County string GeoLocation }

JobPosting represents documents in the nycjobs Azure Search index, as described by NYCJobsWeb/Schema_and_Data/nycjobs.schema. ZipCode represents location documents in the zipcodes index, described by NYCJobsWeb/Schema_and_Data/zipcodes.schema. They are independent index documents; the application uses geographic coordinates to filter job postings rather than a persisted foreign-key relationship. There are no ORM entities, transactions, or repository interfaces.

Caching Strategy

No cache provider, cache annotations, TTL, or explicit query cache was detected. Azure Search SDK clients are held in static fields, but this is client reuse rather than a result cache.

Data Ownership Boundaries

Both indexes are hosted by the same configured Azure Search service. NYCJobsWeb reads from those indexes; DataLoader is the repository's write/provisioning utility and loads the shared index data from local JSON files. No cross-service database access, CQRS, or separate transactional data store was detected.
